routeSelection.basis: The current programme page foregrounds understanding contemporary Russia and its political and economic developments while retaining common Russian-language, historical and cultural foundations. This route therefore best represents the programme's broad academic identity and is also listed first in the current official curriculum; it was selected without reference to UCR fit.

programmes.label: Russian Studies (Russische studies) at Leiden University

exception.reason: The strongest direction—Russian language, literature and cultural worlds—was tested before a history, politics, economy and international-relations direction. UCR offers useful general disciplinary methods in literature, film, media, psycholinguistics, history, sociology, politics, international relations and economics. The current catalogue contains no Russian-language course and no sustained Russia- or Eurasia-specific disciplinary sequence. Russian language and source access are not merely professional qualifications: they organise the external curriculum and connect its literature, history, society, politics and economics. Filling 23 non-PPD places with generic methods would change the object of study to general cultural or international studies. The conclusion rests on complete-programme coherence and actual course content, not title matching or exact module equivalence.
exception.curriculumContext: The settled Politics, History and Economics route remains complete at 180 EC. It preserves the progressive Russian grammar, acquisition and reading sequence, Russian literature and linguistics, the required Daugavpils language/art package, Soviet history, Russian politics, economy and foreign policy, the 10-EC thesis, and two genuine 15-EC open spaces. The zero-credit thesis seminar is excluded. Dutch and English instruction metadata, route selection and first-stage provenance remain unchanged.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 rows in the current enriched UCR workbook, including descriptions or outline-derived profiles, prerequisites and the six cohort availability columns. MCCLITR111, MCCLITR211, MCCLITR311 and MCCLITR312 teach literary interpretation, world literature, adaptation and critical perspectives; MCCMEDI111, MCCMEDI311 and MCCMEDI312 teach film/media, race and documentary methods. MCCMEDI312 mentions Dziga Vertov within a global history of documentary, but one example is not a Russian film or culture sequence. HCBCOGN312 studies psycholinguistics, bilingualism and language acquisition, while MCCCOMM211 studies stylistics; neither teaches Russian, Russian grammar, reading or Russian sociolinguistics. MCCCOMM112 teaches Dutch. GOSHIST111 includes the Russian Revolution, Cold War and the demise of communism in Eastern Europe within a broad modern-history survey; GOSHIST211 treats empires comparatively; GOSHIST312 is a Walcheren Expedition research seminar. These do not establish Russian imperial, Soviet and post-Soviet history progression. GOSPOLI112, GOSPOLI212, GOSPOLI312 and GOSPOLI313 provide comparative-politics, international-relations, public-policy and peace/conflict frameworks; GOSSOCI111/214/311 provide general sociology; BENECON111, BENECON211, BENECON311 and BENECON312 provide economics, international macroeconomics, public economics and econometrics. Their documented content does not supply sustained Russian politics, society, economy or foreign-policy study. No workbook row provides Russian-language acquisition or a Russia/Eurasia area-studies spine. Academic feasibility therefore fails before accepting 24 courses, so no schedule or UCR-credit comparison is fabricated.

candidateAssessment.concept: Russian language, literature and cultural worlds
candidateAssessment.assessment: UCR offers literary, film, media, stylistic and psycholinguistic methods, including an isolated documentary example involving Dziga Vertov. It has no Russian-language instruction and no documented Russian literature, film, visual-art, sociolinguistics or Russian-speaking-world sequence. Generic methods cannot sustain a 23-course Russia-centred programme.

candidateAssessment.concept: Russian history, politics, economy and international relations
candidateAssessment.assessment: Modern history, empire, comparative politics, international relations, sociology and economics supply transferable frameworks. The catalogue does not provide cumulative Russian imperial, Soviet, post-Soviet, political-system, economy or foreign-policy study; a complete programme would become generic international studies rather than a defensible Russian Studies response.
